data.one_liner: An optimized and mature version of Redux for state management in Flutter applications.
data.what_it_does: Holds application state in a central store and updates it via dispatched actions that can execute synchronous or asynchronous logic. Widgets can rebuild using context extensions to read or select state portions.
use_when: You prefer a Redux architecture for managing app state in Flutter
You need advanced async action handling with built-in mixins like debounce, throttle, and retry
avoid_when: You prefer stream-based architectures like BLoC
You want a zero-boilerplate dependency injection and state solution like Riverpod
strengths: Simple to learn and easy to use compared to traditional Redux
Rich set of built-in action mixins for retry, debouncing, throttling, and polling
Powerful testing support and debugging capabilities
weaknesses: Requires writing explicit action classes for state updates, which can involve more boilerplate than simpler providers
Tied to the Redux pattern concept

alternatives.name: bloc
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose bloc if you prefer event-driven, stream-based state management with separate BLoC and Cubit classes.

alternatives.name: riverpod
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose riverpod for compile-time safe, global state management without needing context for provider lookups.

alternatives.name: provider
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose provider for lightweight dependency injection and basic inherited widget state wrapping.
